claims.text: A design system is a product's shared design tokens, ready-made components, rules for using them and their documentation, so each screen reuses decisions instead of making them again.

At stage-2 ProductListScreen, ProductDetailScreen, CreateOrderScreen and OrderDetailScreen each write loading as const Center(child: CircularProgressIndicator()) and a load error as Center(child: Text(...)).

claims.text: At stage-2 spacing is raw numbers: ProductDetailScreen uses EdgeInsets.all(16) and SizedBox(height: 16), CreateOrderScreen SizedBox(height: 16) and SizedBox(height: 8), ProductTile EdgeInsets.all(12); the product name uses textTheme.headlineSmall.
CreateOrderScreen styles the server error as Text with TextStyle(color: Theme.of(context).colorScheme.error); the centered load-error texts of the screens set no style.
A color read from Theme.of(context).colorScheme follows the ThemeData in force above the widget, so changing the theme changes it without editing the screen.

claims.text: At stage-2 DonHang.App has no shared widget for loading or error, no written usage rule and no documentation of its visual decisions (DonHang.App/README.md is Flutter's template text).

claims.text: A design system pays off when several screens or apps must look alike and change together; for a single screen a shared component only adds a file to read.
Extract a shared component after a piece repeats on a few screens, when real uses show which parts are the same; building it before then tends to add a parameter per screen's exception.
The drawing file shows the decisions, but the tokens, components and rules that make every screen follow them live in the app's code.
git switch --detach <tag> checks out the commit the tag points to with a detached HEAD.
